about.title: Cerritos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Cerritos sees a steady flow of traffic where SR-91 meets I-605, and along South Street and Artesia Boulevard, corridors that carry commuters through Los Angeles County every day. Public records show 316 injury collisions and 407 injured people in the most recent year, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons as weekend traffic builds. When a collision happens on these roads, the moments right after matter: photos, witness names, and vehicle positions can fade or disappear fast. We handle car accident claims on a contingency basis, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless you recover. Whether your crash happened at a light on Artesia or in the merge lanes near SR-91, a free case review costs you nothing and starts the process of protecting what you're owed.

items.title: Time Is Limited
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the crash date to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government vehicle or entity was involved. Contacting us early helps make sure that deadline isn't missed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a Cerritos crash, you may still recover a portion of damages. Our team can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement right after a crash — you're not required to give one, and it can be used against you later. We can handle that communication so you don't have to.

items.question: What should I do after a crash near SR-91 or I-605 in Cerritos?
items.answer: Get medical care first, even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up later. Take photos of the scene, vehicles, and any visible injuries, and get names of witnesses if you can. Avoid giving a recorded statement to any insurance company until you've spoken with us.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Cerritos car accident?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government-owned vehicle, like a city or county vehicle, was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. It's worth contacting us early so nothing slips past the deadline.

items.question: Is there a charge to review my case?
items.answer: No — our initial case review is free. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to contact us and ask questions about your situation.
